classification.difficultyReason: The methods are specified; the student links integer-root testing, successive factor extraction and quadratic factorisation to complete the quartic.

content.prompt: Use trial and error to find as many integer zeroes of $P(x)=2x^4+x^3-14x^2+5x+6$ as possible, then use long division to find the other factors.

answer.short:
Integer zeroes: $1,2,-3$.
$P(x)=(x-1)(x-2)(x+3)(2x+1)$; the remaining zero is $-\frac{1}{2}$.
answer.worked:
Possible integer zeroes are factors of $6$:
$$\begin{align*}P(1)&=2+1-14+5+6=0\\P(-1)&=2-1-14-5+6=-12\\P(2)&=32+8-56+10+6=0\\P(-2)&=32-8-56-10+6=-36\\P(3)&=162+27-126+15+6=84\\P(-3)&=162-27-126-15+6=0\end{align*}$$
Thus the integer zeroes are $1,2,-3$.
Long division by $x-1$ gives quotient $2x^3+3x^2-11x-6$ and remainder $0$:
$$\begin{array}{r|l}&2x^3+3x^2-11x-6\\\hline x-1&2x^4+x^3-14x^2+5x+6\\&\underline{-(2x^4-2x^3)}\\&3x^3-14x^2+5x+6\\&\underline{-(3x^3-3x^2)}\\&-11x^2+5x+6\\&\underline{-(-11x^2+11x)}\\&-6x+6\\&\underline{-(-6x+6)}\\&0\end{array}$$
Long division of the quotient by $x-2$ gives $2x^2+7x+3$ with remainder $0$:
$$\begin{array}{r|l}&2x^2+7x+3\\\hline x-2&2x^3+3x^2-11x-6\\&\underline{-(2x^3-4x^2)}\\&7x^2-11x-6\\&\underline{-(7x^2-14x)}\\&3x-6\\&\underline{-(3x-6)}\\&0\end{array}$$
Factorise the quadratic $2x^2+7x+3$ using PSF: Product $ac=2\times3=6$, Sum $7$, Factors $1$ and $6$.
$$\begin{align*}2x^2+7x+3&=2x^2+x+6x+3\\&=x(2x+1)+3(2x+1)\\&=(x+3)(2x+1)\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}P(x)&=(x-1)(x-2)(2x^2+7x+3)\\&=(x-1)(x-2)(x+3)(2x+1).\end{align*}$$
The remaining zero is $-\frac12$.
